questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code handles a failed upload attempt that used an idempotency key? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
What guarantees that exactly one of two simultaneous first-time callers with the same key proceeds to write the blob?
choices: ConcurrentHashMap.merge is atomic per key, and only the caller whose fresh Entry instance is returned gets an empty Optional
The BlobStore serializes writes by path
Each user can only have one request at a time

questions.prompt: A client retries a request whose first attempt fully succeeded. What does it receive?
choices: 200 with the original fileId and no second blob write

questions.prompt: Two different users upload with the identical idempotency key string. What is the effect?
choices: They share one registry entry, so one user's upload is treated as the other's retry
Both writes go to the same blob path
They are tracked independently, because the registry key is prefixed with the user ID
